item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed Dec. 3, email states
item.description: Nidal Hasan is set to die by firing squad in what will be the first military execution since 1961.

item.title: Why you just got a $90 Social Security check — and who missed out
item.description: Millions of seniors are getting $90 direct deposits from Social Security this week, prompting questions about the source of the money.

item.title: Paramount closes $110 billion deal to acquire Warner Bros. Discovery
item.description: The merger unites two major movie studios, news operations CBS News and CNN and cable networks including Comedy Central and TNT.

item.title: Millions of seniors receiving $90 deposits from Social Security Administration
item.description: Roughly 20 million Medicare enrollees are receiving $90 checks this week from the Social Security Administration as part of an effort from President Trump to lower healthcare costs. CBS News' Megan Cerullo reports.

item.title: White House defends Trump's comment to let Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego
item.description: The White House is defending President Trump after he suggested letting Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego. CBS News' Nikole Killion has more.

item.title: Storm brewing off Mexico could impact Gulf Coast as hurricane this weekend
item.description: Tropical Depression Nine formed in the Gulf, and it's expected to become a hurricane later this week.

item.title: Former Cornell students dragged into alleged rape scandal, ask school to clear their names
item.description: A group of former Cornell students say they've been falsely connected to the alleged 2024 fraternity house rape. CBS News' Lilia Luciano has the details.

item.title: The life and travels of an alleged Chinese agent
item.description: A CBS News investigation reveals new details about the life and background of a California mom accused of conducting surveillance for China.

item.title: Yellow labs make first leaf pile jump of this fall season
item.description: Jody Hartman rakes his leaves into a big pile, and then gives his dogs Stella and Mabel the go-ahead to jump in. Tony Dokoupil has the story.

item.title: 7th person arrested after security incident at U.S.-run airbase in England
item.description: British police say they've arrested a seventh person in connection with a security incident at a U.S.-run military base in England, a 22-year-old man suspected of plotting terrorist acts. CBS News' Charlie D'Agata has more.

item.title: Video shows deadly school bus crash in Florida, 911 calls released
item.description: Warning: Disturbing video. New video shows a view from inside the school bus that crashed in Florida on Monday, killing two people, including a girl in 10th grade. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: What audiences could expect from Paramount-Warner merger into Skydance
item.description: CBS News' parent company, Paramount Skydance, merged with Warner Bros. Discovery on Tuesday, creating a new company now called Skydance. Jo Ling Kent reports on what this means for audiences.

item.title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan to be executed by firing squad, Pentagon says
item.description: The Trump administration has approved a plan to execute former Army Maj. Nidal Hasan — who killed 13 people in a 2009 shooting at Fort Hood — by firing squad, the Pentagon said.

item.title: Disturbing details on arrest of California couple who had 21 kids removed from their home
item.description: A California couple has been arrested on child abuse charges after 21 children, many born through surrogacy, were removed from their property. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has more.

item.title: Video shows cheerleader shoved to the ground by police
item.description: Video shows a former Arizona State University cheerleader being shoved and pinned to a bicycle by officers and then being placed under arrest. Carter Evans reports.

item.title: Cornell brings in former DOJ official to lead review of its response to alleged sexual assault
item.description: Cornell University, facing growing criticism of how it handled allegations of a 2024 gang rape in a fraternity house, has hired a former top Justice Department official to lead what it calls an independent review. Lilia Luciano has more details.

item.title: Student protests in France turn violent, leading to thousands of arrests, mostly of teens
item.description: Around 250,000 people protested funding cuts in France that have left public schools with leaks, rats and not enough desks. Aiden Stretch reports on the demonstrations that have turned violent.

item.title: California couple at center of surrogacy scandal arrested
item.description: Guojun Xuan and Silvia Zhang, who had at least 25 children via surrogates, were arrested at their home in Arcadia, California.

item.title: New book from former commerce secretary examines Cuba, Hispanic cultural identity in U.S.
item.description: Former U.S. Secretary of Commerce Carlos Gutierrez has written a new book that argues it's a mistake to think of Hispanic identity as a self-contained ethnicity. Gutierrez joins "The Takeout" to discuss "Sheer Will: Learning to Lead When There is No Path."

item.title: Christa Pike is conscious, speaking after botched execution, attorneys say
item.description: Christa Pike, a death row inmate who was subject​ to a failed execution attempt in Tennessee last week, is conscious and speaking from her hospital bed, her attorneys said Tuesday.

item.title: Gulf Coast under tropical storm threat
item.description: A roughly 700-mile stretch of the Gulf Coast from Louisiana to the Florida Panhandle is under a tropical storm threat, and forecasters warn the storm could intensify into a hurricane, the first of the season in the Atlantic. Rob Marciano has more.

item.title: Tennessee woman conscious, speaking after execution attempt, lawyers say
item.description: Christa Pike, the convicted killer who survived two lethal injections last week in Tennessee, is now conscious and speaking, according to her lawyers. Tom Hanson reports.

item.title: Prosecutors in surrogacy scandal arrest call mansion a "house of horrors"
item.description: A Chinese-born couple was arrested in California on Tuesday, more than a year after 21 children were discovered inside their castle-like mansion near Los Angeles. They are accused of what the L.A. County district attorney calls "horrific punishment and beatings and child abuse." The kids were almost all born via the largely unregulated world of surrogacy and are now in protective custody. Jonathan Vigliotti reports.

item.title: Why Trump now says his PAC will pay for government-funded ads
item.description: President Trump said Monday that his super PAC will start paying for the controversial taxpayer-funded "Love Me" ads the White House recently rolled out. Political strategists Erin Maguire and Chris Meagher join "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Trump suggests letting Iran "take out" LA, San Diego during rally
item.description: Gov. Gavin Newsom called President Trump "deranged and dangerous" after he suggested letting Iran "take out" Los Angeles and San Diego.

item.title: 2026 midterm election races to watch
item.description: CBS News has identified 10 key Senate and 42 House races that will likely decide the majority — all of which can change during the midterm campaign.

item.title: Potential tropical storm brewing over Gulf of Mexico, could hit U.S. this weekend
item.description: A tropical storm brewing in the Gulf could soon hit the U.S. CBS News' Lindsey Reiser reports.

item.title: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground as Mideast crisis engulfs Yemen
item.description: Iran's Houthi allies deny losing ground to Yemen's Saudi-backed military, but oil prices ease despite the Middle East crisis erupting in a battle over control of another key waterway.

item.title: Former Cornell frat members ask university to clear their names
item.description: Some former Cornell University students say they are being falsely connected to a 2024 sexual assault​​ and targeted online.

item.title: Ex-CIA official found with $40 million in gold bars admits to sprawling scheme
item.description: A former CIA official admitted to inventing fake classified programs to divert nearly $200 million in government money that was used to buy Florida mansions and gold bars.
